# Incident Report: 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.17.0.99 |
| MAC | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (domain bepositive.com) |
| Logged-in user | afletcher (confirmed via Kerberos CNameString, frames to/from 172.17.0.17) |

Confirmed via DHCP (option 12 hostname `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT`, client MAC `18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4`), NBNS (`DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>`, `<20>`), ARP (MAC bound to 172.17.0.99), and Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString `afletcher` originating from 172.17.0.99. Domain controller is 172.17.0.17 (WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com).

## Malware Family

**Koi Stealer** — **signature-confirmed**. The provided Suricata/IDS alert export contains a direct hit: `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2`, 172.17.0.99 → 79.124.78.197, TCP 80, matching 48 packets. This is corroborated behaviorally in the pcap: repeated `POST /foots.php` and `GET/POST /index.php` to a bare-IP host (79.124.78.197) using a spoofed legacy IE7/Windows 10 user-agent string, sending `application/octet-stream` bodies of the form `<len>|<GUID>|<token>|<base64/binary blob>` — a stealer bot check-in/exfil pattern. The alert file also independently flags this same flow as `ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser 1`.

Traffic begins at frame 1668 (2024-09-04 21:35:07 UTC, ~3 minutes into the capture) and continues in a steady beacon loop through the end of the capture (22:32 UTC). The pcap does not contain the initial delivery/drop (no executable download precedes the first C2 POST), so the infection vector predates the capture start; only post-compromise C2 activity is observed.

Other alerts in the export (SMBv1/NTLMSSP overflow signatures, Kerberos principal overflow) fire on normal AD/domain-join traffic between 172.17.0.99 and the DC 172.17.0.17 and are not evidence of lateral movement or exploitation in this capture — they are generic pattern matches on legitimate NTLM/Kerberos protocol fields, not corroborated by any payload anomaly.

## Indicators of Compromise (grounded in capture)

**C2 endpoint**
- `79.124.78.197:80` — HTTP C2 for Koi Stealer, 591 packets exchanged with victim. Evidence: tcp streams 48–200+ (`POST /foots.php`), stream 51 (`GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U`, `POST /index.php`); confirmed by IDS alert `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2`.

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` — recurring bot check-in/exfil endpoint (POST, ~45 hits observed).
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — gate/registration request; response body: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|` (frame 2227, tcp stream 51).
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` — POST follow-up on the same stream, encrypted binary payload (frame 2236).

**Bot/campaign identifiers observed in traffic** (not classic file/domain IOCs, but grounded artifacts worth recording)
- Bot GUID: `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654` (repeated in every `/foots.php` POST body).
- Subid/campaign tag: `qIOuKk7U` (in the `/index.php` gate URI and response).

**Domains / file hashes / transferred files**
- No malicious domain was queried for the C2 (malware connects directly to a bare IP, consistent with the alert `POST to Dotted Quad`).
- No malware binary transfer was captured (`--export-objects http` over the full capture yields only benign items: Microsoft NCSI connectivity test, an empty Adobe `ProcessMAU.txt`, and the stealer's own encrypted POST/response bodies, which are not standalone files with recoverable hashes). No SHA256 can be grounded from this capture.

## Benign Context (not IOCs)

- `172.17.0.17` / `WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com` — internal domain controller/DNS server, all SMB/Kerberos/LDAP/DCE-RPC traffic here is normal AD activity.
- `23.220.251.149`, `23.220.251.158` (www.msftconnecttest.com), `199.232.210.172`, `199.232.214.172` (ctldl.windowsupdate.com), `184.29.137.96` (x1.c.lencr.org), `23.220.251.47` (acroipm2.adobe.com/Adobe ARM check) — standard Windows/Adobe update and connectivity checks.
- Microsoft/Bing/MSN/Office telemetry and service endpoints (`login.microsoftonline.com`, `*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `*.msn.com`, `www.bing.com`, `officeclient.microsoft.com`, `odc.officeapps.live.com`, etc.) — normal enterprise Windows 10/M365 background traffic.
- `46.254.34.201` (SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`) — plain TLS session, ~719 KB, no IDS alert on it and no corroborating stealer-pattern evidence. Flagged as **unresolved/benign-leaning context**, not an IOC, since it cannot be grounded as malicious from available evidence.

## Incident Summary

The Windows workstation DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (172.17.0.99, MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), logged in as user `afletcher` on the bepositive.com domain, is infected with **Koi Stealer** (signature-confirmed via ETPRO Suricata rule). Starting at 21:35:07 UTC the host began beaconing directly to C2 server 79.124.78.197:80, repeatedly POSTing encrypted stealer data to `/foots.php` and registering via `/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` under bot ID `30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654`, using a spoofed IE7 user-agent, for the remainder of the capture (through 22:32 UTC). The initial infection vector is not present in this capture — only the post-compromise C2 beacon is observed.
